knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Relocation is usually outside the business's control. Recording it is the right response; blaming the trainer or raising prices is not.
Revisiting the goal against progress keeps the reason for joining in view. The other two steps remove that link.
Early and regular check-ins catch dissatisfaction before a member leaves. Price and coaching replacement are not the purpose.

practicalCriteria: Given a list of six departures, the learner sorts each reason as controllable or not, and the assessor agrees the sort
The learner sets a check-in schedule for three new members at weeks two, six and twelve
The learner records one specific controllable change, linked to the largest controllable reason
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop any retention message that makes a health claim
Stop storing exit feedback that contains information the member did not agree to give
